title: Экономия на бармене  (Saving on the Bartender)

segments.t: The austerity measures continue across the restaurant. Nagiyev confronts Kostya the bartender to deliver some bad news. Let's listen closely to their exchange in Russian first, and then walk through each line together.
Now let's go back through the exchange around Saving on the Bartender line by line and unpack how the Russian works.
'I was just doing my job.' The verb for 'were doing' is in the masculine past tense, marked by that 'l' sound at the end.
'We are saving on everything.' Nagiyev delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'save money'.
'We saved on the bartender.' Nagiyev uses the perfective verb meaning 'to save' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'bartender'.
'You cannot fire me.' Kostya chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'can' for the ongoing action, followed by 'to fire'.
'You are fired, idiot.' Dmitry uses the informal singular 'you' here with 'blockhead', as friends and close colleagues do.
'An idiot, huh?' Kostya turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'blockhead' to make the point directly in conversation.
'This is very unfair.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'very much' directly with 'unfairly', combining 'very much' with 'unfairly'.

'The restaurant is in a difficult situation.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'restaurant' directly with 'difficult', combining 'restaurant' with 'difficult' and 'position'.
'Who will pour drinks?' Kostya chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'will be' for the ongoing action, followed by 'to pour' and 'drinks'.
'This is no longer your problem.' Russian omits the present-tense verb 'to be' here, linking 'more' directly with 'problem', combining 'more' with 'problem'.
'Fine, I will leave today.' The phrasing opens with 'good' before bringing in 'will leave' and 'today' to make the point clear.
'That is excellent.' Nagiyev delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'perfect'. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

Kostya realizes he has lost his job as part of the severe cost-cutting strategy. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'just' and 'to do' — you will catch every word right away. See you in the next scene.
